- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot, especially after spikes.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.10) — model is overly conservative, missing downward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to adjust downward quickly; delay in price correction by 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, pushing prices too far from recent mean; true price tends to revert toward 10–15 day average.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate by 1–3% in early cycles (first 5–7 days), then converge — model “overheats” early, then corrects.
- Sentiment-driven drift: when sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.20 for 3+ days), model forecasts rise faster than true price; when sentiment is negative, model underreacts to falling prices.
